easy.explanation: The father says, “Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father.”
easy.q: To whom does the father speak at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: He says, “Forsake ye not my law.”
easy.q: What does the father command his son not to forsake?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Get wisdom, get understanding.”
easy.q: What does the father tell his son to get?

answers: To know understanding and receive good instruction
medium.explanation: He gives good doctrine and urges them to attend “to know understanding.”
medium.q: Why does the father ask his children to listen to his words?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.”
medium.q: What will wisdom do for the person who loves and keeps her?

answers: Lift her up and honor her
medium.explanation: Wisdom will promote and bring honor to the person who embraces her.
medium.q: What does “Exalt her” mean in the context?

answers: One should gain wisdom and then keep and love it
Wisdom can be kept without being gained
Gaining wisdom prevents a person from loving it
challenge.explanation: The father commands both, “Get wisdom,” and “Forsake her not.”
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between gaining wisdom and preserving it?

challenge.explanation: Wisdom preserves, keeps, promotes, honors, and gives “an ornament of grace.”
challenge.q: What benefits does wisdom provide in this passage?

answers: Possessions are more important than understanding
Understanding should be given priority in every acquisition
challenge.explanation: The command places getting understanding above all other acquisitions.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by “with all thy getting get understanding”?

paragraphs.title: The Way of Wisdom versus the Way of the Wicked

answers: The way of wisdom and right paths
easy.explanation: He says, “I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths.”
easy.q: In what way does the father guide his son?

answers: His steps are not restricted, and he will not stumble
easy.explanation: The passage says, “When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.”
easy.q: What happens to the person who follows the way of wisdom?

answers: Avoid it and turn from it
easy.explanation: He commands, “Enter not into the path of the wicked,” and, “turn from it.”
easy.q: What does the father command his son to do concerning the path of the wicked?

answers: It leads to evil, violence, and stumbling
medium.explanation: The wicked do mischief, practice violence, and do not know what causes them to stumble.
medium.q: Why should a person avoid the way of the wicked?

medium.explanation: The path of the just shines more and more until the perfect day.
medium.q: What does “shining light” suggest in “the path of the just is as the shining light”?

answers: It begins in darkness and remains there
It grows brighter until the perfect day
medium.explanation: The path “shineth more and more unto the perfect day.”
medium.q: What progression is described in the path of the just?

answers: The just walk in light, while the wicked walk in darkness
The just practice violence, while the wicked walk uprightly
The just stumble, while the wicked are secure
challenge.explanation: The path of the just is shining light, while the way of the wicked is darkness.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears between the path of the just and the way of the wicked?

answers: Wickedness is portrayed as their continual practice
They always walk in a straight way
challenge.explanation: Their evil conduct is so habitual that they cannot sleep without doing mischief.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the wicked losing sleep unless they have done mischief?

answers: Wisdom removes the need to choose a path
Walking in right paths allows steady steps without stumbling
Wisdom leads a person toward the way of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The wise person’s steps are not straitened, and he does not stumble when running.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect wisdom with confidence?

paragraphs.title: Guarding the Heart and Directing One's Conduct

answers: In the midst of his heart
On the path of the wicked
easy.explanation: The father says, “Keep them in the midst of thine heart.”
easy.q: Where should the son keep the father’s words and sayings?

easy.explanation: They are “life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.”
easy.q: What do the father’s words give to those who find them?

answers: A froward mouth and perverse lips
easy.explanation: He is told, “Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee.”
easy.q: What kind of speech should the son put away?

answers: The issues of life come from it
It prevents the person from seeing
medium.explanation: The passage says, “Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.”
medium.q: Why should a person guard his heart diligently?

medium.explanation: The verse pairs a froward mouth with “perverse lips,” meaning corrupt or crooked speech.
medium.q: What does “a froward mouth” mean in this context?

answers: Consider the path and establish the ways
medium.explanation: He says, “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”
medium.q: What does the father command concerning the path and the feet?

answers: They help make one’s path and actions upright
They remove the need to choose a way
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from guarding the heart and speech to looking straight and walking rightly.
challenge.q: How are guarding the heart and directing speech connected with conduct?

answers: Focus on the right direction and do not turn aside
Look in every direction and change paths
challenge.explanation: The son is told to look straight, establish his ways, and not turn to the right or left.
challenge.q: What is the practical meaning of looking straight and establishing one’s path?

answers: Keeping the words in the heart, guarding the heart, clean speech, and a straight walk
Doing evil, crooked speech, and forgetting the words
Forsaking wisdom, leaving the path, and entering darkness
challenge.explanation: The instruction progresses from receiving and keeping the words to guarding the heart, avoiding corrupt speech, and walking straight.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in this passage?
